title: Hosted API token lifecycle cost allocator
summary: Working spreadsheet and scenario builder that breaks hosted API unit economics into token lifecycle phases (cold / warmed / cached / amortized), with region-by-region COGS and decision levers for routing, quantization, and burst policies.
purpose: Create an actionable allocator that maps incoming request profiles to marginal and amortized cost buckets so product and ops can (1) prioritize cache/batching investments, (2) pick model quantization targets by SLA tier, and (3) set regional price floors and surge policies tied to cost coverage.
assumptions: GPU hourly costs are amortized over reserved pools; sustained-throughput discounts apply after 72 hours of continuous utilization; KV-cache hit reduces per-token compute by 60% on average; quant-8 reduces GPU cycles by ~28% vs FP16 for generation-heavy workloads; egress and infra network differ by region (NA/EU/APAC).
key_metrics: per_token_marginal_cost, per_token_amortized_cost, ppk_effective, cache_hit_rate, avg_seq_len, model_family, quant_level, region_markup_needed
scenarios:
scenario A: low-latency chat (avg_seq_len=40, cache_hit=10%, quant=FP16)
scenario B: high-throughput embeddings (avg_seq_len=1, cache_hit=0%, quant=INT8)
scenario C: bursty enterprise traffic (sustained windows + preemptible bursts, mixed models)
recommended_levers:
1) Prioritize prefix/KV cache for chat flows where hit rate > 20% — conservative ROI: payback in ~6 weeks on small reserved pool.
2) Route low-seq embedding workloads to INT8 instances in APAC/NA where license+infra cost delta is small.
3) Auto-fallback policy: if dedicated capacity unavailable, route to lower-quant variant with latency-slo guardrails and degrade gracefully.
4) Introduce a regional surge surcharge tied to per_token_amortized_cost + 15% buffer in non-core regions.
action_items:

- Add quantized INT8 profile to model catalog for redwood-7b (owner: Priya)
- Update routing policy to include 'amortized cost threshold' dimension (owner: SRE)
- Run 4-week price-floor simulation for EU region with 3 demand shapes (owner: Finance)
open_questions:
How to account for multi-tenant cache contamination in hosted pools? Currently assumed 15% hit degradation; should validate.
Should we bake license amortization at model-family vs pool-level?
What target margin do we require for enterprise SLA tiers vs free-tier experiments?
notes: This sheet intentionally blends marginal micro-costs (per-token compute) with amortized fixed allocations (reserved GPU pools, license amortization). Use 'marginal' for short tail pricing decisions and 'amortized' for capacity planning and sales pricing. Keep this doc as living: update with real observed throughput and cache metrics after each experiment.
